Report serious abuse or exploitation at work

You’re being seriously abused or exploited at work if you believe you’re being controlled, threatened or manipulated. This could be an indicator of modern slavery.

Reporting modern slavery while on a sponsored work visa

If you’re in the UK on a Skilled Worker visa – which is also known as a Certificate of Sponsorship – and believe you’re a victim of modern slavery or serious abuse at work, contact us by:

the online reporting form

email contact@fairworkagency.gov.uk

These are the quickest routes for investigation. The FWA cannot put you on the National Referral Mechanism without investigating.

Call 999 and ask for the police if you think you are at immediate risk of harm.

Try to include:

what the abuse is

where it’s happening, or happened

any relevant pictures or documents

your name and contact details – we’ll only use these to ask you questions about your report, if needed

You do not need to tell us who you are, but we can support you better if we can contact you.

Information you give will be in confidence and will help protect workers from exploitation.

Reporting by phone

You can also call us if you think you’re a victim of modern slavery.

This can take longer than using the online reporting form or emailing us.

Phone: 0800 432 0804

Calls are free and will be answered between 9am and 5pm, Monday to Friday. You can still call outside of these hours and leave a voice message.

This is not an emergency service number. If anyone is in immediate danger, call 999 and ask for the police.

Complain about problems with pay or work rights

Examples of problems with pay or work rights could include:

working hours

not being paid the National Minimum Wage

an issue with an employment agency

an issue with a gangmaster agency – these are employment providers to agricultural and food processing sectors

Use the complain about pay or work rights form.

Get advice on employment issues

Contact Acas for free and confidential advice to employers, employees and their representatives on employment rights, best practice and policies, and resolving workplace conflict.

Gangmaster licensing

How to apply for or renew a gangmaster’s licence

Check if a gangmaster is licensed

You can call or email the Fair Work Agency if you need advice on gangmaster licensing.

Phone: 0345 161 6000

Email: licensing@fairworkagency.gov.uk

General enquiries

Contact us to:

make a freedom of information (FOI) request

make a media request

complain about the FWA

ask for a document in an accessible format

ask for your personal data (subject access request)

Phone: 0345 161 6000

Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm (except public holidays)

Find out about call charges

Email: contact@fairworkagency.gov.uk

Write to:

Fair Work Agency

Loxley House

Station Street

Nottingham

NG2 3NG

Privacy notice

Our personal information charter sets out how we use your personal data when you write to us.
